title: Sprint 31: compact triage & wireframe notes for intake + cutlist
body:
Context:
This is a compact working doc capturing the sprint-31 triage decisions for the Console intake pipeline and the lightweight wireframes for the new compact cutlist view. Goal is to land a minimal set of UX changes that reduce cognitive load for platform engineers during high-intake bursts and enable faster manual triage of incoming routes. Keep scope small: delivery targeted for the end of Sprint 31 (Feb 26).

Top-level constraints and assumptions:
- Must not add backend schema work beyond an extra boolean on routes ("high_priority") and a new narrow index for intake queue queries.
- Avoid major console nav changes; this is a surface-level panel/overlay.
- Performance: panel must render < 200ms for 100-route queries (server-side paging enabled).
- Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels required for the quick-actions.

Primary user stories (short):
- As a platform engineer, I want a single compact view of top intake signals so I can decide keep/cut/reassign in 2 clicks.
- As a triage lead, I want to pin a small set of routes into a temporary "cutlist" to snapshot changes for sprint planning.
- As an on-call, I want clear indicators for routes currently failing SLOs so I can prioritize fixes.

Compact cutlist requirements (MVP):
1) Row-level compactness: show route name, recent p50 latency (+sparkline), cost per 1k tokens, error rate, last deploy tag. Keep each row to one line with ellipsis for long names.
2) Quick-actions: three contextual buttons (Pin to cutlist, Deprioritize, Mark for follow-up). Each action supports a single keystroke shortcut (P, D, F).
3) Pinning semantics: pinned routes appear in an ephemeral list attached to the sprint context (not persisted to global route metadata unless explicitly saved).
4) Export: ability to export pinned slice as CSV or attach to a JIRA ticket via a modal.
5) Rollout signal: small badge if route has canary rollouts or fallback policies active.

Prioritization matrix (how we decided what to cut):
- HIGH RISK & HIGH COST: must keep in view (not cut). Examples: routes with >5% error rate and cost >$0.10/1k tokens.
- LOW IMPACT & HIGH MRL (maintenance): candidates for decommit.
- LOW USAGE & EQUIVALENT QUALITY: cut from immediate rollout path and schedule for next cleanup.

Compact wireframe descriptions (text sketches):
Screen A — Intake Compact Panel (overlay attached to Console > Routes):
- Header: small search + filter chip row (service, model, region, priority). Right side: "Snapshot to cutlist" button.
- Table area: dense single-line rows. Each row left side: miniature favicon, route name (truncate). Middle: p50 latency value, tiny sparkline (last 24h), cost estimate tag. Right side: error % badge, last deploy tag, three-dot menu + quick-action icons (P/D/F).
- Row hover: reveal inline knob for setting short-term autoscale hint (low/med/high) — this is non-persistent, advisory only.
- Footer: pagination with page size toggle (25/50/100).

Screen B — Cutlist Drawer (right-side slide-in):
- Top: list title + quick save (save to JIRA / export CSV / clear).
- Body: stacked cards (one line) for each pinned route with a short note field (inline editable).
- Actions at card: move up/down, attach to ticket, open route detail.
- Empty state: callout: "No pinned routes — pin from the intake panel with P".

Behavioral details and microcopy notes:
- Quick-action confirmation: instantaneous optimistic UI update; show small undo toast for 5s for destructive actions.
- Pinning: ephemeral by default. Modal when user clicks "Save snapshot" explains the difference between ephemeral and saved (persisted) cutlists.
- Error badge tooltip: "Error rate includes client & server errors; threshold configurable in Project Settings".

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve in sprint):
- Persisted vs ephemeral: do teams want ephemeral-only (fast) or a lightweight persisted cutlist accessible across sessions? (Design leaning: ephemeral first, add save later)
- Autoscale hint control: risk of users misinterpreting non-persistent suggestion as a commit. Need explicit visual hint.
- Keystroke conflicts: confirm with keyboard accessibility audit whether P/D/F conflict with browser or other console shortcuts.

Cutlist for sprint scope (finalized, compact):
- KEEP (do in Sprint 31):
  * Intake Compact Panel (UI + small backend index) — owner: Priya — due: 2027-02-24
  * Cutlist Drawer + export CSV — owner: Jonas — due: 2027-02-24
  * Keystroke shortcuts + undo toast — owner: Ruth — due: 2027-02-22
  * Unit telemetry events for pin/unpin/quick-action (analytics) — owner: Emilio — due: 2027-02-23
- DEFER (parking lot, sketch only):
  * Persisted cutlists with cross-session visibility — move to backlog for Sprint 33
  * Inline autoscale commit flow (requires infra safety checks) — defer
  * Visual diff to compare cutlist snapshots — defer

Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- Intake Compact Panel renders and supports pin/unpin on 25k routes query in <200ms (server paging in place).
- Pinned snapshot export produces CSV with expected columns (route, p50, p95, cost, error%, last_deploy).
- Quick-actions are keyboard accessible and trigger telemetry events.
- No regression for Console routes list default view (feature gated behind "compact-intake-v1" flag).

Testing notes:
- Add automated Cypress flows for pin/unpin, export, and undo toast.
- Manual QA checklist for keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, and color contrast for badges.

Next steps & action items (triage meeting decisions):
- Priya: finalize panel microcopy + handoff sketch to Eng (Feb 12).
- Jonas: prototype drawer interactions in Figma and share interactive link (Feb 14).
- Ruth: coordinate accessibility review and verify keybindings (Feb 16).
- Emilio: add telemetry events schema (ENG-telemetry repo) and wire up test events (Feb 18).
- Samira: create JIRA task for backend index and add to sprint board (PROD-4821) (Feb 11).

Quick links referenced in discussion:
- Intake query perf notes: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/IntakePerf
- Shortcut audit doc: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/shortcut-audit
- Example of compact table pattern: pattern-library/compact-rows

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight — main aim is to reduce decision friction during high-throughput triage. Please point out any UX flows that would imply backend schema changes beyond the single boolean and the narrow index (we want to avoid hidden infra work this sprint).

Changelog (doc edits):
- 2027-02-12: added prioritization matrix and final sprint cutlist (Priya).
- 2027-02-15: wireframe text sketches updated after design sync (Jonas).
- 2027-02-18: added final QA list and dates (Ruth).
